central_claim: Hodgson's military-tribes paper was revised asynchronously by epistemic/documentary layer. In 1857, a new retrospective recruitment footnote was added while older historical and physiognomic base-text readings remained unchanged; later publication states revised those other layers separately.

layers.1857_state: new retrospective footnote explicitly says subsequent experience tested value/availability and regrets earlier recruitment policy was not followed
layers.material_mode: new typeset footnote appended to retained reprint body

layers.revision_timing: no change through 1857; later at least two transformations
caste stable in published tradition for at least 1833-1857 and still present in 1874 base; explicit cast correction is late
layers.source_control: 1832 manuscript reading remains unread; cast may still restore an unpublished early reading, but it does not restore the 1833 printed reading

layers.source_control: absence from correction list does not prove diplomatic identity of every table entry

source_control_rules: Do not collapse a new footnote into a claim that the entire 1857 body was revised.
Do not treat layer-specific change dates as one document-wide revision date.
Do not call cast a restoration until 1832 manuscripts are directly read.
Phoenix target readings remain unread even though transmission predicts likely values.
Absence of a table correction in 1874 apparatus is not proof that no typographic or editorial changes occurred.
